items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And Zill was the guy that was the music director for Louis Armstrong. He wrote this old man Moses day, you know. And so then we opened up in the Savoy in Chicago... later on the mouse played with Cal Calaway.

ctx.x: He'd play music, he'd trance all across the street. It was a novelty, you know. A dancing chicken? Well he'd strut kind of like he was dancing, you know. You could call it a dancing rock. So after that we stayed around Chicago, I mean Milwaukee, and gave our own dances. We would just draw away from the Wisconsin roof, where we was popular, we had been there six years. There was two bands there, Bill Costner's band. Well we wasn't allowed to play any waltzes. We could. But this other band was more on the street or…
What was the name of that band then?
